transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-07 15:00 (ET)
Duration: 48 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Arielle Gomez (Redwood AE), Ben Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Karen Holt (Luminary PM), Ravi Shah (Luminary ML Eng), Jamal Ortiz (Luminary Security), Sofia Li (Luminary Data)

--- OPTIONAL: Auto-generated summary ---
(see 'summary' field above)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Arielle: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio okay?
[00:04] Karen: Yep loud and clear, thanks.
[00:07] Ben: Hi team, Ben here, SE on the pilot, I'll run through the latest quality metrics then we can dig into the bad cases.
[00:15] Ravi: Sounds good. We pushed a small prompt tweak last night, thats the one that's in staging.
[00:20] Ben: Right so I'm looking at the 500-sample weekly sweep - we now have two prompt variations: baseline v1 and constrained v1-b. The constrained prompt reduced hallucinations on slot fill by about 22% but you see there's a small uptick in truncation on long inputs.
[00:38] Sofia: When you say truncation is that during streaming or at generation time?
[00:42] Ben: At generation time, the token budget clips the last sentence, so you lose trailing context. We're seeing it especially on multi-paragraph clinical notes. Might be batching-related.
[00:50] Arielle: Quick context for folks - Luminary's acceptance criteria was set to 0.92 exact for key-entity extraction, or 0.95 fuzzy if reviewer confirms. Is that still accurate, Karen?
[01:01] Karen: That's still the target but we're open to slightly lower exact if practical. Our main worry is false positives in 'medication' slot. We had a false positive yesterday where 'beta blocker' was extracted when it was actually 'no beta blocker'.
[01:15] Ben: Yeah we saw that, sample FPs attached in the spreadsheet. The pattern is negation handling; the model sometimes misses 'no' scope. We tried adding explicit guardrail prompt lines like 'Do not infer if negative qualifiers present', which helped in 60% of cases.
[01:30] Ravi: The guardrail felt brittle in longer notes though, where negation is split across sentences. Could we combine prompt-level guardrails with simple post-filter rules?
[01:40] Ben: Absolutely, a hybrid approach is what we recommend for edge cases — use a 2nd-stage heuristic that looks for negation tokens in the sentence window. We can provide a sample post-filter.
[01:50] Jamal: From security, quick Q: can we force customer-managed KMS for private keys? Our compliance requires tenant-specific keys and audit logs.
[01:59] Arielle: For Private deployments yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Hosted we have bring-your-own-key via a vault option in the roadmap — I'll flag that to the product team.
[02:12] Jamal: Ok please send the SOC2 and KMS architecture doc.
[02:16] Maya: I'll send SOC2 and the audit log spec by Monday.
[02:19] Karen: Thanks.
[02:20] Ben: Back to metrics — I want to call out a regression we saw after switching quantization profile on the dedicated test cluster. It shaved cost but introduced soft tokenization changes, small differences in extraction boundaries. The weekly scoring rig flagged a 3% drop in fuzzy recall for entity spans.
[02:38] Ravi: Did you re-run the evals at same beam/temperature? Could those hyperparam diffs explain it?
[02:45] Ben: We kept temperature and beams identical, it looks like the quant path changes how subword splits appear which shifts span offsets. It's small but enough to affect exact-match counts.
[02:55] Sofia: Are we able to normalize offsets before scoring? We sometimes get penalized for off-by-one tokenization.
[03:01] Ben: Yes, we can do token-boundary relaxation in the scorer — we suggested that in the rubric: exact-match, relaxed-match (1 token tolerance), and normalized-fuzzy (levenshtein threshold).
[03:11] Karen: For acceptance we need to look at both user-impact and reviewer workload. If relaxed-match is high but exact is low, reviewers will still need manual work, so we care about exact for top 10% of cases.
[03:25] Arielle: Good point. Let's map the 10% worst cases to reviewer time estimate — Sofia can you add estimated minutes-per-case for manual review?
[03:34] Sofia: Yep I can do that and attach to the eval CSV.
[03:38] Ben: On the prompt set — we built a canonical set of 42 prompts used across the reg tests. They include edge-case anchors (negation, copied text, truncated notes, abbreviations). I'll push that canonical set to the shared drive, link in next steps.
[03:52] Ravi: Can we also include an obfuscated version of the training prompts to check for leakage?
[03:57] Ben: We'll include a sanitized subset; can't share raw training but we'll provide representative examples.
[04:03] Karen: I wanted to flag two high-risk FPs from the spreadsheet — case A and case B. Case A is false medication; case B is incorrect date inference from note header. Both are showstoppers for clinical workflow.
[04:16] Ben: For Case A we recommend two changes: stronger negative guardrails in prompt + post-filter. For Case B, we can add a precedence rule: if date exists in header use that, don't infer from cognitive context. It's a deterministic rule.
[04:30] Ravi: That precedence rule sounds good. Is that handled in Redwood routing or should we implement it in our preprocessing?
[04:36] Ben: Preprocessing is simplest short-term — you can canonicalize headers before sending. In the longer term we can add pipeline transforms in Dedicated.
[04:44] Arielle: About regressions — Maya, you mentioned nightly runs. What's current cadence and what signals do we alert on?
[04:52] Maya: Nightly regression runs on the staging model generate fail counts plus precision/recall deltas. We alert if fuzzy recall drops >2% or if high-severity FPs >5 in a run. Also we snapshot model artifacts and prompt versions.
[05:06] Karen: Could we get diffs between runs (per-prompt) so we see which prompt caused the drift?
[05:12] Ben: Yes, the per-prompt delta export is available — Ben will attach per-prompt deltas in next deliverable.
[05:18] Jamal: Another compliance Q — retention: how long will logs be kept in hosted? We need 7 year retention option for some audits.
[05:26] Arielle: Hosted default is 90 days for transcripts, but for enterprise we can extend retention and provide exportable audit logs; long-term retention is an add-on. I'll include pricing notes.
[05:36] Karen: Ok. On the scoring rubric, can we walk the team through one sample scoring?
[05:40] Ben: Sure — sample note ID 9832: ground truth meds [aspirin], model predicted [aspirin], exact=1, fuzzy=1; span offset exact=1. Another sample with negation: ground truth none, model predicted 'aspirin' exact=0, fuzzy=0. Score aggregates into F1 across the set, with optional weighted penalty for high-severity fields like medication.
[05:59] Sofia: Weighting sounds right — let's weight medication x2, dates x1.5.
[06:05] Karen: Agree.
[06:07] Ben: One more item — we've added lightweight guardrail injection where we prepend 'only extract when...' instructions. Works for many but not all. It's prompt-architecture dependent.
[06:18] Ravi: What's the impact on latency? Are these big prefixes?
[06:22] Ben: The guardrail adds ~20 tokens sometimes which increases p99 by like 30-40ms on our hosted config. On dedicated with batching it amortizes better.
[06:33] Arielle: Tradeoff summary — guardrails reduce hallucination but increase cost/latency and sometimes interact with quantization. Need to pick acceptable SLOs.
[06:43] Karen: Our SLOs are p95 < 300ms and cost < $0.015 per 1k tokens? That's rough, need to confirm.
[06:52] Ben: We can run a cost-latency sweep and provide suggested batching + cache configs to meet that. We'll include in the deep dive.
[07:00] QUESTION (Karen): If we decide to rollback a model because of regression, what's the process?
[07:04] Ben: Rollback is a route config change — we can pin traffic to previous model, or do instant fallback on error. For Dedicated you can do a canary or traffic split. Rollback time is minutes.
[07:14] Arielle: Okay let's go to the failure examples. Ben, can you read two representative failure traces?
[07:19] Ben: Sure — Failure 1: Note with 'no history of diabetes' where model extracted diabetes=yes. Failure 2: Date inferred from context instead of header. (reads snippets)
[07:35] Ravi: For failure 1, you see the token 'no' was separated by parenthetical note and the model lost scope. Post-filter would look for 'no' within 10 token window.
[07:45] Ben: Right.
[07:46] Sofia: I'm adding reviewer time estimates: FP case ~4-6 minutes to adjudicate.
[07:51] Karen: Given that, we need FP below 1% for meds or reviewer burden balloons.
[07:58] Ben: Understood. We'll tune the guardrail and post-filter.
[08:03] Arielle: Actionables recap coming after this section.
[08:06] Ben: On the scoring rubric attachment — link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/luminary/pilot/score-rubric-v2 (note: internal link).
[08:18] Ravi: Quick ask — can the scoring pipeline produce per-tenant anonymized reports? We cannot send raw PII out.
[08:25] Ben: Yes, the pipeline supports PII stripping and token-level redaction prior to exporting. We'll show config.
[08:32] Maya: I'll include the export steps in the docs I share.
[08:35] Karen: Also, are we using continuous batching? That was an ask earlier to reduce cost while keeping latency.
[08:41] Ben: We can enable continuous batching on dedicated; it helps throughput but increases average latency slightly. For your workload, we can tune batch windows to prefer latency at peak.
[08:51] Jamal: One more security: can we require network egress restrictions so data stays in VPC?
[08:57] Arielle: For Private yes. For Dedicated we have VPC peering options. Hosted is multi-tenant so not possible.
[09:05] Karen: Good.
[09:07] Ben: Ok, jumping to regression controls — nightly run currently tests 1k seeded examples plus 500 random samples from production (sanitized). We diff against baseline and produce per-prompt deltas and a dashboard.
[09:19] Sofia: Are the random samples stratified by note length? We saw drift concentrated in >500 token notes.
[09:25] Ben: Yes stratification exists, but we can increase weight on long notes. That will give earlier signal on truncation regressions.
[09:34] Ravi: If we increase sample of long notes, will that change alert thresholds?
[09:38] Maya: Possibly — we'll re-tune thresholds because variance increases. Suggest we keep current thresholds for now and create a separate long-note alert bucket.
[09:49] Karen: That works.
[09:50] Arielle: Time check — 15 minutes left. Let's confirm the three deliverables and owners.
[09:56] Ben: Deliverable 1: canonical prompt set + sample post-filter rules (Owner: Ben)
[10:00] Ben: Deliverable 2: per-prompt delta export & failure traces (Owner: Ben)
[10:04] Ravi: Deliverable 3: run expanded evals (1k->5k) and share flagged set (Owner: Ravi)
[10:09] Maya: Deliverable 4: SOC2 & audit logs doc (Owner: Maya)
[10:12] Arielle: Add timeline: Ben to share prompt set by 2025-05-09, Ravi to run evals and share by 2025-05-14, Maya to send compliance docs by 2025-05-12.
[10:23] Karen: One last thought — for reviewer UI, can we surface 'why' the model chose a span? Some explainability would help triage.
[10:31] Ben: We can attach attention-ish saliency highlights or token-level scores; not perfect but helpful. We'll include a mockup in the next deck.
[10:38] Sofia: I'll draft reviewer time per-case numbers and attach.
[10:41] Arielle: Great. Any other items?
[10:44] Jamal: No from security aside from docs.
[10:46] Karen: No, that's it.
[10:47] Arielle: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread and share the artifacts.
[10:52] End Recording
